messages.author: b97e7faaa37e3f37
messages.subject: change reference temperature
parts:
Hi INLA team,

I am working on an INLA model to understand the effect of temperature on mortality, where the behaviour of temperature is captured by natural cubic splines with 4 basis functions without intercept. I understand that this can be modelled by a random walk of order 2, but for this example I will like to work with natural splines.

Due to word limit, I have attached the model, code and dataset I have used in the attachments. The result is as follows, but what we find awkward is that by default the reference levels is the minimum temperature. Is there a simple way to change the reference category to say 10oC? We are happy to define this either in the inla call or when making predictions.


Thank you in advance.
Best, Xinyi

messages.author: b97e7faaa37e3f37
messages.subject: change reference temperature
parts:
Hi INLA team,

I am working on an INLA model to understand the effect of temperature on mortality, where the behaviour of temperature is captured by natural cubic splines with 4 basis functions without intercept. I understand that this can be modelled by a random walk of order 2, but for this example I will like to work with natural splines.

My model basically looks like:
form_eg <- deaths ~ 1 +
  offset(log(population)) +
  factor(dow) +
  Temp_matrix +  # temperature
  f(id_doy, model = "rw2", scale.model = TRUE, constr = TRUE, hyper = hyper_rw2) +
  f(id_year, model = "iid", constr = TRUE, hyper = hyper_iid)

where Temp_matrix is specified by
knots <- quantile(sampleData$temperature_lag03,c(10,75,90)/100, na.rm=T)
Temp_matrix <- ns(sampleData$temperature_lag03, knots = knots, intercept = FALSE)

I have used the following code to plot the result:
coeff_inlaEg <- inla_eg$summary.fixed[8:11,]
ns_median <- Temp_matrix  %*% coeff_inlaEg[c(paste0(1:4)),"0.5quant"]
ns_LL <- Temp_matrix  %*% coeff_inlaEg[c(paste0(1:4)),"0.025quant"]
ns_UL <- Temp_matrix %*% coeff_inlaEg[c(paste0(1:4)),"0.975quant"]

The result is as follows, but what we find awkward is that by default the reference levels is the minimum temperature. Is there a simple way to change the reference category to say 10oC? We are happy to define this either in the inla call or when making predictions.

Thank you in advance.
Best,
Xinyi

Hi inla team,

Sorry for this. The inla call is writted as follows:
control.family=inla.set.control.family.default()
inla_eg <-  inla(formula = form_eg,
                  family="Poisson",
                  data=sampleData,
                  verbose = TRUE,
                  control.family=control.family,
#                  control.fixed = list(expand.factor.strategy="inla"),
                  control.compute=list(config = TRUE, dic=TRUE, waic=TRUE),
                  control.mode=list(restart=T),
                  num.threads = round(parallel::detectCores()*.8),
                  control.predictor = list(link = 1))

Best,
Xinyi

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] change reference temperature
parts:
Hi,
I plotted by the following code:

coeff_inlaEg <- inla_eg$summary.fixed[8:11,]
ns_median <- Temp_matrix  %*% coeff_inlaEg[c(paste0(1:4)),"0.5quant"] 
ns_LL <- Temp_matrix  %*% coeff_inlaEg[c(paste0(1:4)),"0.025quant"]
ns_UL <- Temp_matrix %*% coeff_inlaEg[c(paste0(1:4)),"0.975quant"]

coeffSpl_DF_sample <- data.frame(temp03 = sampleData$temperature_lag03,
                        median = ns_median,
                        LL = ns_LL,
                        UL = ns_UL)
ggplot(data = coeffSpl_DF_sample) +
  geom_line(aes(x = temp03, y = exp(median))) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = temp03, ymin = exp(LL), ymax = exp(UL)),
               alpha = 0.3, fill = "blue", col = NA) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, col = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_bw() + xlab("Mean Temperature (lag0-3)") + ylab("Effect") + ggtitle("effect by inla (sample)")

Thank you.
